headline: Across media, gaming, publishing and education, firms show mixed performance with pockets of growth and tightening IT spend.
summary: Media & Entertainment sees strong revenue at Disney but mixed margins at WBD. Gaming revenue is rising at Bally's while Caesars struggles and IT budgets tighten. Publishing blends AI investments at Wolters Kluwer with a revenue miss at Scholastic. Education shows Pearson’s growth against cost cuts at SLU and uncertain spend elsewhere.

industries.summary: Disney posted 8% revenue growth and expanding IT spend. WBD’s margin fell and its IT outlook is tightening. Versant reaffirmed guidance and is expanding digital platforms.

laggards.why: Low 5.2% operating margin and tightening IT spend

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Disney launched AI search summaries and a trip‑planning tool; Wolters Kluwer (see Publishing) added AI decision‑support tools.

themes.title: Digital platform rebuild
themes.detail: Versant added FAST channels and streaming memberships; Disney is merging Hulu into Disney+.

themes.title: Cost pressure
themes.detail: WBD is cutting staff and consolidating studios to save costs.

industries.it_note: IT spend is expanding at Disney and Versant but tightening at WBD; account teams should balance AI opportunities with cost‑control.

industries.summary: Bally's revenue surged 21.7% with expanding IT spend. Caesars posted a net loss despite modest digital growth. Light & Wonder and Brightstar signal tighter budgets.

leaders.why: Revenue up 21.7% YoY and expanding IT spend

laggards.why: Revenue down 3.5% YoY and tightening IT outlook

themes.title: Digital revenue growth
themes.detail: Caesars saw digital revenue rise 5% YoY; Bally's digital EBITDA also improved.

themes.title: Debt reduction focus
themes.detail: Light & Wonder prioritises debt reduction; Brightstar cites rising debt pressure.

themes.title: AI support messaging
themes.detail: Caesars emphasizes AI will support, not replace, in‑person meetings.

industries.it_note: Bally's is expanding IT for integration, while Light & Wonder and Brightstar are tightening; monitor budget shifts.

industries.summary: Wolters Kluwer expands AI tools and IT spend. Scholastic missed revenue and posted a large loss. Pearson shows strong revenue growth and expanding IT.

leaders.why: Revenue of $1,779 m and expanding AI‑driven credential platform

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer acquires AgileMD and launches Blue Chip IQ AI; Pearson expands Credly credentials.

themes.title: Cost restructuring
themes.detail: Pearson announced a major business restructure to improve margins.

themes.title: Neutral reporting
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer released a half‑year report with no major sentiment shift.

industries.it_note: AI‑focused projects drive IT expansion; account teams should highlight AI integration opportunities.

industries.summary: Pearson reports accelerated revenue growth and expanding IT spend. SLU cuts custodial staff, indicating tightening. NYU and ACT show unclear IT direction.

leaders.why: Revenue growth and expanding AI credential platform

laggards.why: Outsourced custodial services and layoffs signal cost cuts

themes.title: AI credential growth
themes.detail: Pearson’s Credly platform saw a 506% rise in AI credentials over two years.

themes.title: Cost‑cutting measures
themes.detail: SLU outsourced custodial work and laid off staff; Pearson also announced a restructure.

themes.title: Community data‑center focus
themes.detail: NYU highlights expectations for community‑focused data‑center services.

industries.it_note: Pearson expands IT for AI services, while other institutions face unclear or tightening budgets; tailor outreach accordingly.
